title: Pasta with tomato-based sauce, seafood, and added vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: A home recipe for pasta tossed in a tomato‑based sauce, assorted seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) and added vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, spinach). The pasta is cooked al dente, while the sauce is slightly spicy, enriched with garlic and basil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato sauces in Italian cuisine are traditionally made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, and fresh herbs.
Seafood is a rich source of omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart health.
The pasta‑seafood combination is popular along the Mediterranean coast, especially in coastal Italy.
Adding vegetables boosts fiber content and makes the dish more filling without extra calories.
Homemade sauce retains more vitamins than store‑bought versions.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Seafood and pasta together provide a complete amino‑acid profile that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Omega‑3 from fish and antioxidants from tomatoes help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes supply vitamin C and lycopene, vegetables add vitamin A and folate, seafood contributes zinc and iodine.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain pasta aid digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Using durum‑wheat pasta results in a slower rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the sauce is made with canned tomato puree or broth, salt levels can be high.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Seafood must be cooked thoroughly to avoid bacterial contamination.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten; gluten‑free alternatives are needed for celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, topped with the tomato‑seafood‑vegetable sauce. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or a drizzle of olive oil. The dish pairs well with a light white wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to keep the sauce from drying out. Only the sauce (without pasta) is suitable for freezing.
